behavioral_notes.observation: A dashboard is a stored o-spreadsheet document: spreadsheet.dashboard inherits spreadsheet.mixin, which persists the workbook as JSON (spreadsheet_data) plus a binary copy. The readonly data route calls _get_serialized_readonly_dashboard(), which json.loads(spreadsheet_data), injects the user's locale (res.lang._get_user_spreadsheet_locale) and the company currency (res.currency.get_company_currency_for_spreadsheet) into settings, attaches an empty revisions list and the translation namespace, and returns it as the snapshot the OWL client hydrates into an o-spreadsheet Model in mode:'dashboard'. The cells contain ODOO formulas (pivots/lists/charts bound to business models) that the data provider re-evaluates client-side — the 'BI' content is data, not Python.

Metadata-invisible 'empty state' behavior: main_data_model_ids (Many2many to ir.model) declares which business models a dashboard reports on. The data controller checks _dashboard_is_empty() — it sudo-reads each declared model and, if any has search_count([],limit=1)==0, treats the dashboard as empty and instead serves a static demo workbook loaded from sample_dashboard_file_path (file_open + json.load), flagged is_sample:true. So a fresh database with no live records renders a canned sample dashboard rather than blank figures.

spreadsheet.dashboard.group is the catalog/section layer (Finance, Sales, HR, Website, Services, Logistics, Marketing seeded in data/dashboard.xml); published_dashboard_ids is a domain-filtered One2many ([is_published=True]) the client lists. Visibility is enforced by ir.rule, not the controller: record rule ir_rule_spreadsheet_dashboard restricts base.group_user to dashboards whose group_ids intersect the user's groups ([('group_ids','in',user.all_group_ids.ids)]); spreadsheet_dashboard_rule_company adds a multi-company filter on company_ids; the Dashboard 'Admin' group (group_dashboard_manager) bypasses via [(1,'=',1)]. _unlink_except_spreadsheet_data blocks deleting a group that carries a non-export external_id (i.e. shipped by another module).

Public sharing snapshots a dashboard: action_get_share_url() creates a spreadsheet.dashboard.share (a frozen spreadsheet.mixin copy), zips any provided xlsx exports into excel_export, and returns full_url = .../dashboard/share/<id>/<uuid-token>. The public portal route renders spreadsheet.public_spreadsheet_layout with is_frozen and props.dataUrl=/dashboard/data/<id>/<token>. Access is double-gated by _check_dashboard_access: consteq() constant-time token compare AND the share creator (create_uid) must still have read access to the source dashboard, else werkzeug Forbidden. Download (xlsx) additionally requires base.group_allow_export.

The viewer is a substantial OWL app, not a view: SpreadsheetDashboardAction (action 'action_spreadsheet_dashboard', registered force:true, lazy-loaded via addSpreadsheetActionLazyLoader) renders a ControlPanel + sidebar of groups/sections + SpreadsheetComponent in dashboard mode, with global filters (SET_GLOBAL_FILTER_VALUE), favorites toggle, URL sync (router.pushState dashboard_id) and a mobile variant (DashboardMobileSearchPanel, MobileFigureContainer, DashboardSearchBar, DashboardFacet, DashboardDateFilter). A reactive 'spreadsheet_dashboard_loader' service webSearchReads the published groups, lazily fetches each dashboard's JSON over http.get('/spreadsheet/dashboard/data/<id>'), builds the o-spreadsheet Model with an OdooDataProvider that re-evaluates cells on data-source-updated, and clears on action change. Two o-spreadsheet patches add chart-granularity controls (ChartDashboardMenu) and dashboard chart animations (ChartJsComponent). None of this is reverse-engineerable from Python metadata (gap #3).

it_architecture.application: spreadsheet_dashboard (BI/analytics dashboard layer on the spreadsheet engine: stored o-spreadsheet workbooks + OWL dashboard viewer)
software_services: /spreadsheet/dashboard/data/<dashboard> (serialized readonly dashboard snapshot, with sample fallback)
information_flows: depends: spreadsheet (provides spreadsheet.mixin: spreadsheet_data JSON, binary copy, action_edit_dashboard, xlsx zipping)

render: OWL SpreadsheetDashboardAction -> spreadsheet_dashboard_loader.load -> webSearchRead spreadsheet.dashboard.group -> http.get /spreadsheet/dashboard/data/<id> -> o-spreadsheet Model (dashboard mode) with OdooDataProvider re-evaluating ODOO() formulas
data binding: dashboard cells reference arbitrary business models (pivots/lists/charts) via main_data_model_ids; empty -> static sample workbook from sample_dashboard_file_path
share: action_get_share_url -> create spreadsheet.dashboard.share (frozen copy + zipped xlsx) -> public /dashboard/share/<id>/<token> -> public_spreadsheet_layout (is_frozen)
frontend_components: SpreadsheetDashboardAction (OWL client action, dashboard viewer root)

capabilities: Author & Store BI Dashboards as Spreadsheets (workbook persisted as JSON via spreadsheet.mixin)
Organize Dashboards into Groups/Sections (Finance, Sales, HR, Logistics, ...)
Render Interactive Read-Only Dashboards (OWL viewer: global filters, charts, pivots, lists)
Bind Dashboard Figures to Live Business Data (cells reference arbitrary models via ODOO formulas)
Serve Sample/Demo Dashboards on Empty Databases (sample fallback)
Control Dashboard Visibility by Group & Company (record rules)
Publicly Share & Export Dashboards (token-gated portal + xlsx download)
value_streams: Author-to-Publish: design spreadsheet dashboard -> assign group + visibility/company -> is_published -> appears in viewer
View-to-Insight: open viewer -> load published groups -> fetch dashboard JSON -> hydrate o-spreadsheet model -> re-evaluate ODOO formulas against live data -> rendered figures
Share-to-External: action_get_share_url -> frozen share snapshot + token URL -> public portal render / xlsx export
policies: ir_rule_spreadsheet_dashboard: users see only dashboards whose group_ids intersect their groups
spreadsheet_dashboard_share_create_uid_rule: a share is owned by its creator (create_uid = user.id)
share access double-gated: constant-time token (consteq) AND creator still has read access; xlsx download requires base.group_allow_export
_unlink_except_spreadsheet_data: cannot delete a group shipped by another module
stakeholders: Business user / analyst (consumes dashboards, applies filters, favorites)
Module developer (ships dashboards + sample data, extends the OWL viewer)
External recipient (views/downloads a shared dashboard via public token URL)
metrics: LOG_DATASOURCE_EXPORT telemetry on print/export of a dashboard
The dashboards themselves are the metric surface (KPIs/charts/pivots over business models) — this module is infrastructure FOR metrics, not a metric owner

classification.rationale: spreadsheet_dashboard is firm-infrastructure / BI-tooling (Porter support activity; Stabell & Fjeldstad 'support'). It produces no primary value in any single chain/shop/network — it is a horizontal analytics-presentation layer reused across apps (Finance, Sales, HR, Logistics, Services, Marketing, Website groups are all seeded), depending only on the generic spreadsheet engine and binding to whatever business models a dashboard's cells reference (main_data_model_ids). Its substance is the FRONTEND (14 JS files, the OWL SpreadsheetDashboardAction viewer + reactive loader service + o-spreadsheet chart patches) plus 3 thin models and 4 routes that just serialize a stored workbook — a presentation/decision-support layer, not a transactional document chain. APQC 13.0 'Develop and Manage Business Capabilities' is chosen because the module delivers the analytics/KPI-dashboard capability that lets the organization measure and improve its other capabilities (13.0 covers managing business performance / the enterprise's measurement and improvement tooling). 8.0 'Manage Information Technology' was considered (it is technical platform code) but rejected: unlike `web` (a generic UI runtime that is pure IT delivery), this module's purpose is business-performance visualization — packaged BI dashboards consumed by analysts to make decisions — which is a business-capability/performance-management concern (13.0) sitting on top of the IT platform rather than IT delivery itself.

standard_capabilities: Spreadsheet-based BI dashboards (pivots, lists, charts, scorecards) authored in o-spreadsheet
Dashboard grouping/sectioning with publish flag and sequence ordering
Read-only interactive viewer with global filters, date filters, favorites, mobile layout
Group- and company-scoped visibility via record rules
Sample/demo dashboard fallback on empty databases
Public token-based dashboard sharing + xlsx export
Locale/currency-aware rendering injected at serve time
typical_fits: Shipping curated dashboards per app (the spreadsheet_dashboard_* sibling modules add account/sale/hr/pos/website dashboards into the seeded groups)
Restricting a dashboard to a security group and/or company out of the box
Sharing a frozen dashboard externally via a public link without granting backend access
common_gaps: Authoring a new dashboard's spreadsheet content / ODOO formulas (requires the spreadsheet editor + data modeling, not config)
Custom OWL components or new dashboard widgets beyond the shipped viewer (JS dev, gap #3)
Scheduled/push distribution of dashboards (email/snapshot) is not in this module
No external BI/integration surface here (gap #7) — 0 HTTP call sites; data stays inside Odoo
drive_hints: odoo shell: env['spreadsheet.dashboard.group'].search_read([], ['name','sequence']) to list the seeded sections
odoo shell: d = env['spreadsheet.dashboard'].search([('is_published','=',True)], limit=1); d._get_serialized_readonly_dashboard()[:200] to see the snapshot the viewer hydrates
curl GET /spreadsheet/dashboard/data/<id> (auth=user, cids cookie) to fetch a dashboard payload (or the is_sample fallback)
odoo shell: env['spreadsheet.dashboard.share'].action_get_share_url({'dashboard_id': d.id, 'spreadsheet_data': d.spreadsheet_data}) to mint a public share URL, then GET it
